title: Post-Selection Welfare-Divergence Bands along a Kullback-Leibler Penalty Path
banked_reason: D0.5 graded the honest penalty-indexed softmax result incremental with paper_score_ceiling 6 below the field floor 7.4; the divergence-indexed inverse upgrade was exhausted twice, and four bounded panel findings remain unrepaired.
gap_reasons: The note proves a uniform influence law, multiplier tube, quadratic-regret process, and softmax monotonicity result, but these are smooth fixed-dimensional indexed-inference extensions of published fixed-penalty results rather than a distinct field-level framework.

The foldwise nuisance-rate events are assumed rather than derived from primitive learner/model conditions; discharge conditional rates for the actual fold learners or explicitly rescope the theorem conditionally.
The proof asserts |hat e-e|<=1 after a lower-only epsilon/2 clip, but no upper range restriction on hat e is declared; add an upper clip/range condition or remove this false bound.
Its Taylor reduction invokes uniform interiority to set gradient M_c(theta_c)=0, but ass:uniform-interior is absent from depends_on; add it (or a declared FOC lemma) to the DAG route.
Theorem-level related-work comparisons for the post-selection tube remain incomplete.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 proved the central foldwise multiplier-replacement theorem after repairing its dependency closure, then established the penalty-indexed uniform influence law, shared multiplier tube, quadratic-regret process, population divergence-slope dichotomy, and conservative set-valued inversion. Two targeted maximality rounds attempted to add a smooth sample inverse, uniform Bahadur expansion, cancellation-based fixed-divergence welfare law, and simultaneous band; both workers declined that theorem as unproved and retained only the honest fallback. D0.5 therefore capped novelty at incremental, with the foldwise-rate setup, propensity-clipping bound, uniform-interiority dependency, and related-work comparison still requiring repair before reuse.
tldr: On the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass of FangRidderXie2026, with \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), every maintained optimizer path is either identically the benchmark rule or has a divergence derivative uniformly bounded away from zero on \(\mathcal C\). The established joint uniform influence law and shared conditional multiplier process yield a simultaneous welfare--divergence tube indexed by penalty and valid after any measurable selection of the displayed penalty. Eventwise set-valued inversion reports all welfare values compatible with a selected divergence without requiring a derivative or branch choice; it remains the safe construction for the constant path or any nonregular extension. The Hessian quadratic form separately calibrates the \(n\)-scaled penalized-regret process.
gap: FangRidderXie2026 Theorem 1 gives the efficient influence function and bound, Theorem 2 gives the fixed-penalty quadratic-regret law, Theorem 4 treats estimated-propensity IPW, and Theorem 5 gives the efficient doubly robust optimizer and quadratic-regret limit, all at fixed optimization penalty \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}>0\). With \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), hence \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), and with its admissible rules restricted to the common finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass \(\{\pi_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\), it does not supply joint inference over the direct penalty path \(c\in\mathcal C\). Generic orthogonal-band theory assumes rather than verifies the uniform estimated-influence replacement needed for fold-specific learned influences evaluated along the same-sample implicit optimizer path.
fill: The project states the stronger path-uniform interiority, three-derivative smoothness, and curvature conditions explicitly; derives their finite-action softmax sufficient-condition routes; proves product-bias, sum-radius, path plug-in, envelope, and entropy bounds for the empirical replacement condition; uses a measurable ridge fallback that equals ordinary Hessian inversion uniformly with probability tending to one; obtains the joint uniform influence and shared-multiplier laws; forms a conservative simultaneous tube; and calibrates uniform second-order regret. The inverse correspondence is obtained afterward by direct application of RenTelschowSchwartzman2024.
